title: The Caspian Sea
text: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland body of water, often classified as a lake due to its lack of connection to the ocean. It borders five countries: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, and Azerbaijan. The Caspian covers an area of approximately 371,000 square kilometers and has a length of about 1,200 km. Its surface is about 28 meters below mean sea level. The Caspian is fed primarily by the Volga River, which contributes about 80% of its inflow. It is known for its sturgeon population, historically the source of beluga caviar, though overfishing and pollution have severely depleted stocks. The region contains significant oil and natural gas reserves.
